title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-jackson-hall
content:
Quick scratchpad for negotiation talking points and clauses to watch. Personal notes - not final.

Context:
- Customer: mid-market fintech, wants Dedicated + Private during pilot.
- Using our standard Inference Services Agreement as starting point (see Confluence link).
- They flagged three areas: liability cap, data processing / outputs ownership, SLA credits and incident response.

Key clauses to watch / redline notes:
1) Liability cap / consequential damages
- Current template: cap = greater of $1M or 12 months of fees. Customer asking for higher cap and carve-outs for IP infringement.
- Risk: higher cap increases exposure across Dedicated deployments.
- Talking point: propose amendment to 1x ARR for Dedicated customers after negotiation, otherwise keep template. For pilot, stick to template but add explicit carve-out language limiting punitive damages.
- Suggested redline language: carve-out only for gross negligence/willful misconduct; no carve-out for ordinary business losses.

2) Data processing & ownership of outputs
- Customer wants ownership of model outputs and derivative models. They are pushing 'work product belongs to customer'.
- Our standard: customer owns input data; outputs owned by customer but model weights and improvements remain Redwood IP. We also need rights to use de-identified telemetry for quality/improvements (with option to opt-out for Private deployments).
- Negotiation point: for Private deployment, offer an explicit opt-out for telemetry + written commitment to anonymize; for Hosted/Dedicated require opt-in for product-improvement data usage.
- Suggested redline: add explicit definition for "Output Data" and clause: "Customer owns Output Data; Redwood retains all rights in Service Improvements and Model Weights. Redwood will not use Customer Output Data to train foundation models without explicit written consent. Telemetry may be used in aggregated, de-identified form for debugging and performance monitoring unless customer opts out in writing."

3) Confidentiality & reverse engineering
- They want broad language prohibiting reverse engineering. Fine, but need carve-out for benchmarking and security research by our ops teams and partners (subprocessors).
- Add exception for internal debugging, security testing, and compliance-related reverse engineering with NDA-level protections.

4) Security obligations / compliance / audit rights
- They request SOC2 + penetration test reports and audit rights on infrastructure. For Private we can provide architecture diagrams and SOC2 attestations; we cannot allow broad on-site audits of Redwood-hosted infra.
- For Dedicated/Dedicated-on-customer-cloud: allow annual security questionnaire + redacted SOC2 report. For Private on-prem: allow customer to run agreed security checks after scheduling and under NDAs.
- Suggested redline: limit audit scope and require notice, mutually agreeable auditor, and reasonable timelines.

5) SLA / credits / service levels
- Template: uptime SLO with credits capped at % of monthly fees. Customer wants lower latency SLOs and financial penalties for misses.
- We usually offer performance targets for Dedicated with defined credits but not unlimited liability.
- Negotiation: clarify measurement windows, exclude force majeure, and require customer to demonstrate reproduction steps. Consider operational playbook (runbook) appendix describing incident handling.

6) Termination for convenience / transition assistance
- Customer wants long transition assistance and IP transfer of tuned model checkpoints. We should be careful: tuned checkpoints may contain Redwood proprietary techniques.
- Offer 90-day transition assistance and export of Customer Data + Output Data; do not export Redwood model weights or internal checkpoints. If customer pays for bespoke fine-tuning rights, negotiate separately.

7) Indemnities / IP infringement
- Template: mutual indemnities limited to willful infringement. Customer wants broader seller indemnity.
- Counter: stick to standard mutual indemnity; provide stronger language for third-party data claims if we have explicit indemnity from vendor of model weights.

Open items / TODOs:
- Ask infra/SRE for realistic latency numbers for Dedicated GPU pool (p50/p95) to include in SLA appendix. (@Avery)
- Confirm telemetry opt-out process for Private deployments with product (Maya).
- Legal: confirm acceptable cap floors for enterprise deals (what's min $ cap acceptable for Sales).
- Check with applied-ml on whether we can offer a "model-tuning export" product at price X for customers wanting checkpoint transfer.

Negotiation playbook (short):
- Start with template. If customer insists on higher liability cap, ask for balanced protections: higher cap only for direct damages and exclude punitive/consequential; require higher revenue commitment in contract.
- On data usage: prioritize explicit opt-out for telemetry and promise not to use Output Data for training without consent. Offer paid add-on for training/transfer.
- SLA: define runbook + playbook + reasonable credits. Avoid open-ended penalties.
- Audits: provide SOC2 and redacted reports; restrict on-site audits.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language simple - customers often throw in legalese. Pull examples from recent HubSpot and Stripe deals (ask Sales).
- Watch for "customer may use results for any purpose" - we should allow them business use but protect model IP.
- Remember to add clause about export controls / sanctioned entities if fintech customer processes payments cross-border.

Sample quick redlines to paste into doc (skeletal):
- "Telemetry and Improvements: Redwood may collect performance telemetry and de-identified usage data for the purpose of providing and improving the Service. Redwood will not use Customer Output Data to train foundation models or for model commercialisation without Customer's explicit written consent. For Private deployments, Customer may elect to opt out of telemetry collection in writing."
- "Limitations of Liability: Except for liability arising from (i) gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (ii) infringement of a party's intellectual property rights, each party's total aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of $1,000,000 or the fees paid by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim."

Bottom line: keep the three buckets negotiable: (1) cap & indemnity, (2) data/telemetry/outputs, (3) SLA/incident handling.

Timestamp: 2026-02-14 11:22 - updated after chat with Avery.

End of scratchpad.
